title: E0104: HTTP Response Splitting
plain_english: Writing user input to HTTP headers without sanitizing CRLF sequences (`\r\n`) can allow an attacker to inject additional headers or split the HTTP response.
why_matters: HTTP response splitting can: - Inject malicious headers (for example `Set-Cookie` or `Location`) - Enable cache poisoning - Enable cross-site scripting (XSS) in some contexts - Bypass security controls
what_it_checks: `header()` calls with tainted input that may contain CRLF sequences
`setcookie()` with tainted values that may contain newlines
